mainTopic: Who inherits first: the grandfather (אבי האב) or the brother of the deceased? Then the opening of the משנה about the three portions taken by בנות צלפחד.
overview: The amud opens with a short answer explaining why a sharp sage missed a point in the משנה: his quick mind made him skip careful study. Then רמי בר חמא asks a question. If עשו dies, who inherits first: his grandfather אברהם or his brother יעקב? רבא tries to answer from the משנה, 'the father comes before all his descendants.' The גמרא explains that רמי בר חמא read that line as covering only a father's own children, not his grandchildren. It then proves from the משנה's rule, 'whoever comes first in inheritance, his descendants come first,' that יעקב takes the place of יצחק. So the brother inherits before the grandfather. Finally, a new משנה begins: בנות צלפחד received three portions of land. These were their father's own portion as one who left מצרים, his share in his father חפר's estate, and the extra share he got as a בכור.

steps.title: Why a sharp sage missed the point
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers an earlier question: the sage was so sharp that he did not look carefully at the משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because of his sharpness, he did not look into it carefully.
steps.whatsHappening: This line finishes a discussion from before this section. It explains why a certain sage ruled in a way that seems to clash with the משנה: his quick, sharp mind made him skip careful study of it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא had asked how this sage could rule against an explicit משנה. The answer does not defend his ruling. It explains the mistake: being quick can lead a person to overlook details.

keyTerms.meaning: he did not look carefully, did not analyze

phrases.english: Because of his sharpness
phrases.notes: This answers a question asked earlier on the daf, about a sage whose ruling seemed to go against the משנה.

phrases.english: he did not look into it carefully.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes a discussion from before this section.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains the error instead of defending the ruling
steps.terutzMaskana: The sage simply overlooked the משנה because of his quick mind.

steps.title: Grandfather or brother: who inherits first?
steps.stepSummary: רמי בר חמא asks whether the deceased's grandfather or his brother inherits first, using אברהם and יעקב inheriting עשו as the example.
steps.simpleTranslation: רמי בר חמא asked: the father's father and the brother, like אברהם and יעקב with עשו's property, which of them comes first?
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic begins. רמי בר חמא asks a real question: when a man dies with no children and no living father, does his grandfather inherit, or his brother?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both relatives reach the deceased through his father (יצחק in the example). The grandfather is one step above the father. The brother is one step below him. So it is not obvious which one is 'closer.'

keyTerms.meaning: comes first, has priority in inheritance

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the practical rule for the order of inheritance between a grandfather and a brother.

phrases.english: Rami bar Ḥama asked:
The father's father and his brother –
phrases.notes: 'His' means the deceased: his grandfather versus his brother.

phrases.english: such as Abraham and Jacob, regarding Esau's property,
phrases.notes: אברהם is עשו's grandfather and יעקב is his brother. Their link is יצחק, who in this case is no longer alive.

phrases.english: which of them comes first?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new question, unrelated to step 1.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the grandfather or the brother of the deceased inherits first.

steps.title: רבא answers from the משנה
steps.stepSummary: רבא quotes the משנה: the father comes before all his descendants, so אברהם would come before יעקב.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Come and hear: the father comes before all his descendants.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא tries to answer רמי בר חמא's question from a line in the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא reads 'all his descendants' broadly, so it includes grandchildren. יעקב is a descendant of אברהם, so by this reading אברהם inherits first.

keyTerms.meaning: his descendants (literally, those who come out of his thigh)

phrases.english: Rava said: Come and hear:
The father comes before all of his descendants.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers an answer to the question in step 2.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The grandfather (אברהם) comes first, based on the משנה.

steps.title: Why did רמי בר חמא ask at all?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: surely רמי בר חמא knew this משנה, so why was he unsure?
steps.whatsHappening: In only three words, the גמרא asks why רמי בר חמא had a question if the משנה seems to answer it. This sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A great אמורא would not have missed a משנה. So he must have read it differently from רבא. The next step explains his reading.

phrases.english: And Rami bar Ḥama?
phrases.notes: The גמרא is asking: how could רמי בר חמא ask this, if the משנה already answers it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions how רמי בר חמא could ask in light of רבא's proof.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the משנה clearly says the father comes first, the question has no reason to exist.

steps.title: Only his own children, not his grandchildren
steps.stepSummary: רמי בר חמא read the משנה as saying the father comes before only his own children, not before his son's children.
steps.simpleTranslation: His own descendants, but not his son's descendants.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains רמי בר חמא's reading. The משנה only says a father comes before his own children, so it does not settle the grandfather-versus-grandson case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By this reading, יצחק comes before his children for עשו's estate. The משנה says nothing about אברהם against יצחק's children. So רבא's proof falls away, and the next step settles the question from a different line of the משנה.
steps.confusionAlert: Here 'the father' in the משנה means the deceased's own father (יצחק), not the grandfather. Mixing up the generations is the easy mistake in this סוגיא.

phrases.english: his own descendants,
and not the descendants of his son.

steps.triggerLanguage: יוֹצְאֵי יְרֵיכוֹ שֶׁלּוֹ וְלֹא יוֹצְאֵי יְרֵיכוֹ שֶׁל בְּנוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 4, and in doing so rejects רבא's proof from step 3.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: 'All his descendants' may mean only his direct children, not grandchildren.
steps.terutzMaskana: רמי בר חמא read 'the father comes before all his descendants' as covering only his own children, so the משנה did not answer his question.

steps.title: Proof that the brother comes before the grandfather
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא supports רמי בר חמא's reading from the משנה's rule 'whoever comes first, his descendants come first.' Since יצחק would beat אברהם, יעקב beats אברהם too.
steps.simpleTranslation: So too it makes sense, since it teaches: This is the rule: whoever comes first in inheritance, his descendants come first. If יצחק were alive, יצחק would come first. Now too, when יצחק is not alive, יעקב comes first. Learn from it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a proof from another line of the משנה. It shows that רמי בר חמא's reading is correct, and that the brother (יעקב) inherits before the grandfather (אברהם).
steps.deeperAnalysis: A father inherits his son before the grandfather does, so יצחק would beat אברהם. The rule says that whoever comes first passes his place on to his descendants. So יעקב, יצחק's son, takes יצחק's place and beats אברהם.

keyTerms.meaning: so too it makes sense (a supporting proof)
learn from it; the point is proven

steps.whatToRemember: The brother of the deceased inherits before the grandfather, because the brother stands in the place of their father, who would have come first.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the practical order of inheritance: the deceased's father's descendants come before the deceased's grandfather.

phrases.english: So too it makes sense, since it teaches:
This is the rule: anyone who comes first in inheritance –
his descendants come first;
and if Isaac were alive, Isaac would come first,
phrases.notes: יצחק is עשו's father, and a father inherits before a grandfather.

phrases.aramaic: הַשְׁתָּא נָמֵי דְּלֵיתֵיהּ יִצְחָק – יַעֲקֹב קוֹדֵם;
phrases.english: now too, when Isaac is not alive, Jacob comes first;
Learn from it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Backs up רמי בר חמא's reading from step 5 and settles the question from step 2.
steps.raayaObject: רמי בר חמא's narrow reading, and the ruling that the brother comes before the grandfather
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה's general rule: whoever comes first in inheritance, his descendants come first
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: יעקב (the brother) inherits עשו before אברהם (the grandfather).

steps.title: בנות צלפחד took three portions
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה: בנות צלפחד received three portions of land: their father's own portion, his share of his father חפר's estate, and an extra share because he was a בכור.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: בנות צלפחד took three portions in the inheritance: their father's portion, since he was among those who left מצרים; his portion with his brothers in חפר's property; and, because he was a בכור, he takes two portions.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It lists the three portions of ארץ ישראל that בנות צלפחד inherited from their father.
steps.deeperAnalysis: צלפחד had a portion of his own as one of those who left מצרים. He also had a share in his father חפר's estate. Because he was a בכור, he got a second, extra share of that estate. His daughters inherited all three.

keyTerms.meaning: our משנה (the start of a new משנה)
firstborn son, who inherits a double portion

phrases.english: MISHNA: Zelophehad's daughters
took three portions in the inheritance:

phrases.aramaic: חֵלֶק אֲבִיהֶן – שֶׁהָיָה עִם יוֹצְאֵי מִצְרַיִם,
phrases.english: their father's portion, since he was among those who left Egypt,
and his portion with his brothers in Hepher's property,
and since he was a firstborn, he takes two portions.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ בְּנוֹת צְלָפְחָד נָטְלוּ שְׁלֹשָׁה חֲלָקִים בַּנַּחֲלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a new משנה, separate from the discussion above.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בנות צלפחד received three portions: their father's own portion as one who left מצרים, his share in חפר's estate, and his extra share as a בכור.
